says: One person founds two Teams both named 'Platform' (team.found twice: two ids). Team A is founded on the desktop, whose device is its finalizer; its instructions source is observed in the desktop's clone and committed there, and the laptop accepts them as a Team package (transfer.stage, transfer.accept). Team B is founded on the laptop with its own source and no environment adopted. Earlier work runs in Team A on the laptop: a start composed, selected and activated in a Claude Code session (returning the instructions projection it routed), and that conversation opened as a recipient link scoped to Team A. Team A's recent history (operation.history.read) holds one checkpoint, that activation's receipt, noting an old goal. Then the laptop is partitioned from the desktop: Team A is offline. The launcher (surface.drive) lists both Teams by name with a short id apart; Team A is selected because the recipient is bound to it and shown remote_unknown, not current or adopted because its package is held here. Down and Enter browse Team B: browse_scope becomes Team B while selected_scope stays Team A and the recipient link stays the same, and Team B's view shows its environment checked_empty. Only Space selects Team B's instructions, and then selected_scope is Team B. Tab and Enter dispatch one start whose preparation.compose basis is Team B alone; route.select records Team B's route. Negative: the two Teams are never merged, as every scope, route and request names one id; browsing Team B changes neither the selection nor the conversation, which stays linked to the offline Team A; Team B's missing environment neither blocks its selection nor borrows Team A's; the Team B start carries nothing of Team A's source or history; the repository location selects no Team; Team A's checkpoint and old goal never assign Team A or that goal to current work; and a selection naming the Team by its shared name instead of a route id is refused at admission (pattern_mismatch /selected).
